messages:
incident-bot: [P1] Multiple warmup failures observed for model redwood/ultra-13k in us-east-1c. Symptoms: container init crashes, repeated CUDA OOM during model load, and sporadic nvrtc kernel compile failures. Triggered 2026-03-15T11:03:19Z. Paging oncall.

kai (oncall): ack, I'm taking the page. Bringing lina/ben/harpreet in. What's the initial scope?

lina (ml-eng): grabbing the failing pod logs from pod infer-ultra-2b:
```
[E] 11:03:12 load_model_shard: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (error 2)
[E] 11:03:13 deserialize_weights: unexpected EOF while reading tensor data
[E] 11:03:14 nvrtc: kernel compile timed out after 45s for fused_attention
```

lina (ml-eng): note that this model has aggressive fused kernels enabled by default. We shipped a runtime change yesterday that increased JIT parallelism for compile throughput. suspect the parallel compiles + large tensors are exhausting device memory during init.

ben (sre): impact summary: 18 inference pods failed warmup across three host pools; approx 8 customers show elevated 5xx on first request, two are high-SLA customers. Autoscaler attempted to create replacements but they also hit init OOMs and got backoff.

harpreet (platform): short-term mitigations proposed:
  - set REDWOOD_JIT_PARALLELISM=1 for affected deployment (force serial compile)
  - bump model init timeout to 120s to allow longer compile on older drivers
  - enable software fallback to non-fused kernels (REDWOOD_FORCE_FALLBACK=1)
  - temporarily route new traffic to redwood/ultra-6k variant

kai (oncall): which can we flip quickly? lina, can we runtime toggle without full rollout?

lina (ml-eng): yes, we have a per-model env override via model-config map. Patch is low-risk: reduces concurrency of nvrtc jobs. Command:
```
kubectl -n redwood patch configmap model-config-ultra --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/data/JIT_PARALLELISM","value":"1"}]'
kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deploy/inference-pool --selector=model=ultra
```

ops-bot: scheduling rolling restart for pods with label model=ultra across us-east-1c. ETA ~3 minutes.

harpreet (platform): I'm also pre-creating warm standby nodes with larger GPU-reserve (reserve 2Gi for driver/JIT) in us-east-1c so new pods have headroom.

ellie (cust-succ): drafting customer message for impacted tenants: short note explaining transient warmup failures, mitigations applied, estimated recovery 15-30m. Holding until we validate canaries.

kai (oncall): canary update: after model-config patch, 4/4 canary pods warmup successfully in 2 minutes. 5xx on first requests from affected customers dropped from 6.2% -> 0.9%.

ben (sre): telemetry: hosts with nvidia-driver 535.* still show sporadic nvrtc timeouts. hosts on 545.* do not. We'll avoid scheduling canaries to 535.* for now. Also increasing init timeout to 120s to catch slower compiles.

lina (ml-eng): additional change: enable streamed deserialization to avoid holding full tensor buffers in GPU simultaneously. Patch in progress; it's a slightly larger change but will reduce peak memory during load.

deploy-bot: hotfix rollout: ulthotfix-20260315-2 by lina  applying configmap JIT_PARALLELISM=1 and REDWOOD_FORCE_FALLBACK=0 for canaries.

kai (oncall): customer note approved, send now. ellie, include guidance that traffic may be routed to smaller model if we detect recurrence. mention INC-2026-046.

ellie (cust-succ): sent to affected customers. one reply: "Thanks — please let us know if we should switch to a hot-standby endpoint." I suggested we can route them to ultra-6k now; they asked to be notified before any routing changes.

ben (sre): plan for next 30m: monitor error rate and GPU memory usage. If stable (<1% warmup 5xx) for 15m, we'll scale the patch to the rest of the pool. If regressions occur, we'll enact forced fallback to non-fused kernels and increase node driver pool with 545.x.

kai (oncall): handing off to ben in 20m. leaving runbook notes: suspect JIT parallelism + driver combo. TL;DR: reduce parallelism, increase init timeout, route to fallback model if needed.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-2026-046  mitigations applied (JIT parallelism reduced and warm standbys provisioned). Error rate decreased; monitoring for 15m before further rollout. Next update or any regression will trigger immediate page.
